title: dart-libp2p crashes (unhandled exception) when a peer resets a UDX connection
description: Found in Phase 7. When js-libp2p aborts a libp2p connection over UDX (RESET_STREAM + CONNECTION_CLOSE, error code 1), the dart-libp2p host process dies: 'Unhandled exception: UDXTransportException: UDX operation failed: Stream reset by peer with error code: 1 (context: UDXP2PStreamAdapter(2).data.onError, transient: false)'. The error is rethrown from the adapter's data stream onError (dart-libp2p lib/p2p/transport/udx_stream_adapter.dart) with nothing listening, so any remote peer that resets a connection can take down a Dart node. Repro: js-udx tools/dart-libp2p-peer listen; js-libp2p dials it and idles ~20 s (its connection monitor aborts the connection because of jsudx-aof), or any abort. Fix belongs in dart-libp2p: surface the reset as a stream/connection error instead of an unhandled async exception.
close_reason: Fixed in dart-libp2p branch fix/yamux-fin-on-window-update (a2f03a0 yamux FIN on WINDOW_UPDATE routed through the DATA path; da01036 close completers marked handled so a reset no longer crashes the host; regenerated stale udx_stream_adapter_test mocks). dart-libp2p full suite: same 54 pre-existing failures as main, +23 passing; js-udx interop.test.ts half-close, idle (45 s) and new reset-survival tests pass against it and fail against dart-libp2p main. Not merged.

title: dart-libp2p Yamux ignores FIN on WINDOW_UPDATE frames (no half-close from Go/JS)
description: Found in Phase 7 (libp2p interop over UDX). dart-libp2p lib/p2p/transport/multiplexing/yamux/stream.dart _handleWindowUpdateFrame only applies frame.length to the send window; it never checks YamuxFlags.fin. go-yamux and js-libp2p's @chainsafe/libp2p-yamux (stream.js sendCloseWrite) send their half-close as WINDOW_UPDATE|FIN with length 0, so a Dart stream never sees EOF from Go or JS peers: read() keeps waiting, an echo handler never finishes, and the peer's read-until-EOF stalls. Not transport-specific (TCP too). Dart<->Dart works because Dart sends FIN on a DATA frame. Repro: js-udx tools/go-libp2p-peer dial <dart-libp2p-peer listen addr> 1000 -> 'CORRUPT read: i/o deadline reached after 1000 bytes'. Fix belongs in dart-libp2p: handle FIN (and probably ACK/SYN) flags on WINDOW_UPDATE the same as on DATA (mark remote closed, wake readers). js-udx Phase 7 tests read exact lengths instead and keep an it.fails case for this.
notes: Also kills idle js-libp2p<->dart-libp2p connections after ~20 s: js-libp2p's connection monitor pings every 10 s and closes each ping stream's write side; Dart never sees that FIN, so the ping stream stays half-open, the second heartbeat hits ping's maxOutboundStreams (1) and the monitor aborts the connection (TooManyOutboundProtocolStreamsError). Go peers are unaffected.
close_reason: Fixed in dart-libp2p branch fix/yamux-fin-on-window-update (a2f03a0 yamux FIN on WINDOW_UPDATE routed through the DATA path; da01036 close completers marked handled so a reset no longer crashes the host; regenerated stale udx_stream_adapter_test mocks). dart-libp2p full suite: same 54 pre-existing failures as main, +23 passing; js-udx interop.test.ts half-close, idle (45 s) and new reset-survival tests pass against it and fail against dart-libp2p main. Not merged.

title: go-udx: acknowledge PINGs sent under a nonzero sequence
description: Next up (before Phase 5). go-udx never ACKs PING-only packets (not data-bearing), so dart-udx ping() and js-udx ping()/PMTUD probes always fail against Go; dart-libp2p's relayed-connection health check then waits 5 s and falls back to a test stream. Fix in ../go-udx on a branch: in Connection.HandlePacket, treat a packet with a PING frame and Sequence != 0 as ack-eliciting (immediate ACK via noteReceived with edge=true); keep seq-0 PINGs (go-udx's own control packets) unacknowledged so ACKs never elicit ACKs. Mirror js-udx connection.ts handlePacket rule. Add go tests; then js-udx go-interop test 'ping resolves false against Go' and 'datagramSize stays 1418' must flip (ping true; PMTUD rises to 1472). Merge locally, don't push.
close_reason: go-udx fix/ack-pings (7867fb6, merged 92446f8, not pushed): numbered PINGs/probes recorded and ACKed at once; seq-0 PINGs unacked. go tests in ack_policy_test.go; js-udx go-interop now asserts ping()=true and PMTUD=1472 (fails against pre-fix go-udx).

title: Graceful connection close drops received-but-unread stream data
description: Closing a connection aborts every stream at both ends (stream.abort -> finish clears readQueue), so bytes the peer has received and acknowledged, even with its FIN, are lost if its reader is paused at that moment. Found writing examples/backpressure.ts: sender did end(); await flushed(); close() while the receiver paused 10 ms per MiB -> receiver's iterator threw ConnectionClosedError(code 0, remote) with data unread. Docs now tell users to wait for the receiver to end its side first (doc/streams.md, doc/connections.md#closing). Same risk in libp2p-udx: UdxMultiaddrConnection.sendClose waits for flushed() (ACK level), and a receiver that has paused the UDX stream for backpressure drops the buffered tail. Possible fix: on a NoError remote close, let a stream whose FIN and all bytes up to finalSize have arrived deliver its buffer and end normally. Check go-udx/dart-udx behaviour first.

title: js-libp2p: paused stream's async iterator drops buffered data on remote close-write
description: @libp2p/utils 7.4.1 AbstractMessageStream[Symbol.asyncIterator] ends its pushable on 'remoteCloseWrite'. If the reader has paused the stream (e.g. @libp2p/utils echo() waiting for 'drain'), bytes still in readBuffer are dispatched as 'message' after resume(), but the iterator's output has already ended, so they are silently lost. It should end on 'end' (maybeDispatchEnd fires it once readBuffer is empty and the remote closed). Transport-independent repro with @libp2p/utils streamPair: reader pauses 50 ms after its first chunk while the writer sends 1 MiB and close()s -> 'received 65536 of 1048576'. Seen in Phase 7 as go-libp2p dialing js-libp2p's echo(): Go's echo came back 262144 of 1048576 then EOF. Upstream report to libp2p/js-libp2p not yet filed (outward-facing; ask the user). js-udx tests use an echo handler that never pauses.
notes: Reported upstream 2026-10-02 as https://github.com/libp2p/js-libp2p/issues/3646 (by stephanfeb), with streamPair repro and a verified fix (end the iterator on 'end' instead of 'remoteCloseWrite'). js-udx tests keep the non-pausing echo until a fixed @libp2p/utils ships.

title: UDX interop under netem (loss/delay/reorder) in Docker
description: Phase 5 follow-up. Run the JS<->Go and JS<->Dart interop (tools/go-peer, tools/dart-peer, tools/bulk-peer via UDX_BULK_PEER) under netem loss/delay/reorder, reusing go-udx/interop's Dockerfile.netem + netem-run.sh.
